changes.to: 1.2.0 (refit: 48 of 100 abilities, 10 single-step stat changes, no price raised)

evidence: batch_0009 (400 games, T2 mirror, ai 1.2.0): ability usage rises monotonically with price - 9.3% mean use at 0 AP, 17.6% at 1 AP, 39.6% at 2 AP, 54.9% at 3 AP; 13.3% at cooldown 1 up to 44.2% at cooldown 3. 47 of 100 abilities are used in under 5% of the rounds where they are affordable and have a legal target. Reproduced in batch_0007 and batch_0008.
hypothesis: The inversion is a pricing artefact, not 47 weak kits. Under whole-card cooldown every ability spends the same activation, so the budget's generous credits (-3 per AP, -2 per cooldown round) let expensive abilities buy large gross while cheap ones stay too weak to be worth an activation. Cutting the credits, raising the per-ability floor and capping R against the basics should flatten usage without making anything more expensive to cast.
success_metric: In the next T2 mirror batch: the gap in mean usage between 0-AP and 3-AP abilities falls from 45.6 points to under 25, and fewer than 25 of 100 abilities sit below 5% use.
revert_if: Median game length leaves 10-14 rounds, or any champion's win-rate CI falls outside [30, 70], or mean AP generated per team-round moves by more than 25%.
side_effects: R gross falls from 13.1 to 9.9 on average, so burst ultimates are weaker and fights should last longer - which also pushes median game length back up toward the 13-18 target. The roster loses its 9 HP tier (three champions drop to 8) and gains two speed-2 champions, so tanks are slightly less durable and two carries slightly slower. Champion win rates will move; that is expected and is not evidence against the patch unless a CI leaves [30, 70].

batches.held_constant: rules 1.1.0 corrected, ai 1.2.0, T1 mirror, 150 games each

success_metric_2.target: fewer than 25 of 100 abilities below 5% use

champion_ci_outside_30_70.note: about 60 games per champion here, so these are wide intervals; champion balance is Phase 4 work and was not this patch's target

result.reading: Pricing was the cause of the inversion and the recalibration fixed it: usage no longer rises with price, and if anything now tilts the other way. The abilities that stay below 5% are a different problem - they are situational effects (REVEAL, shields, blinks) that the policy rarely finds a use for, which is an AI-or-kit question for Phase 4 rather than a pricing one.
